2G|148.Measurement Name: Node RX Quality and RX Level
2G|148.Measurement Name in previous release: Node RX Quality and RX Level
2G|148.Measurement Description: Node RxQuality and RxLevel Measurement (M148) reports the received signal quality and signal level information both in uplink and downlink directions for the node of the composite cell (CMST).The RX Quality part registers received signal quality information. The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The counters give the distribution of these samples divided to each quality band. The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels (TCHs).The RX level part registers information on the level and quality of RX signal. The RX level is provided in six subclasses per RX quality band in both uplink and downlink directions. There are 48 counters corresponding to the RX quality bands defined in both uplink and downlink directions. The incrementation is made according to the number of each RX level class received by the BSC in the radio link measurement messages. RX level is divided into six subclasses in both uplink and downlink measurements and the ranges of the classes are set by the user with the RXn parameter of the measurement 53 RX Level Statistics, for example 0-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-30, 31-40, 41-63. In the RX level counter incrementation the missing radio downlink measurement reports and the BTS measurement averaging parameter are taken into account. If the downlink measurement is missing, the latest downlink measurement is used. This way the counters are updated every 480 ms.

2G|149.Measurement Description: Node Handover Adjacent Cell Measurement (M149) collects counters about how handovers between different cells are divided. Counters are updated when the handover is performed to the adjacent cells from the node of the serving Composited Multisite Transmission (CMST) cell. Counters are collected for maximum 78 adjacent cells. One set of counters are collected for adjacent cells if more than 78 adjacent cells are recorded during the measurement period. BTS and Node identifications of the serving CMST cell are in the measurement header object part and adjacent cell identifications are in the counter part. The measurement includes counters for handover attempts, successful handovers, and counters for failed handovers.

In EC-GSM IoT Measurement Coverage Class mapping 
- UL TBF counters shall be updated with used UL CC. Counter shall be mapped for    BTS/CC object accordingly.

When Abis LAPD multiplexing is used with the BTSPlus, counters cannot be collected per each single multiplexed D-channel separately. Instead, one of the D-channels acts as a master channel and the statistics of all the multiplexed D-channels are collected on that channel.

2G|513.Measurement Description:
STM-1 Interface Measurement (M513) The STM-1 Interface Measurement monitors the ability of different hierarchical levels of SDH/SONET connection to provide agreed quality at the speed of STM-1/OC-3 per SDH/SONET Exchange Terminal (SET). The measurement provides information about the amount of Errored Background Blocks (EBB), amount of Errored Seconds (ES), amount of Severely Errored Seconds (SES), and amount of Unavailable Seconds (UAS). The measurement counters are collected from the SDH/SONET termination equipment on physical interface (SET). The measurement identifier is 513/201H.

The object is SDH/SONET exchange terminal (SET) that is identified by the exchange terminal type (SET) and index. There are also counters for SDH/SONET paths terminated to a certain SDH/SONET exchange terminal. In case VC-12 over VC-4 mapping is used, the STM-1/OC-3 interface contains one path, the counters of PATH1 are updated and others are left to zero. In case VC-12 over VC-3 or VC-11 over VC-3 / VT1.5 over STS-1 mapping is used, the STM-1/OC-3 interface contains three paths and all path counters are updated. n be used.

There is a restriction in defects that effect far-end counters. If there is a near-end SES caused by near-end defect then far-end path at same stage is assumed error free. This is because the far-end error indications and counts got from SDH/SONET frame are possibly corrupted because of near-end defects.

In case the terminology is different according to the regulations of American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI), both ANSI and ETSI versions are used in the document, divided with '/' (for example, STM-1/OC-3).

2G|661.Measurement Description:
M3UA Association Set Measurement (M661) The M3UA Association Set Measurement (295H/661) can be used to monitor MTP3 User Adaptation Layer (M3UA) traffic. It provides information on traffic throughput and quality of M3UA connections, as well as M3UA layer and M3UA Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) layer traffic.

M3UA layer counters tell the payload of the SCTP connection. From the counters of the SCTP layer, the operator can follow the traffic of the SCTP layer used by M3UA association. The SCTP layer counters give the operator more accurate information on real load required for sending M3UA traffic through SCTP by including a number of retransmitted SCTP packets and SCTP header. Unavailability counters can be used for fault monitoring, for example, if the association is in ASP-INACTIVE state. The measurement is configured by using interface T2 MML command group commands.
